hypothesis: Theorems AF-1 and AF-2 (paper papers/abstraction_frontier/paper.md) predict, on the 4-bit Boolean world with the shared-through-Z task family (parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}, parity{0,1,2,3}), that the Pareto frontier over the four axes (task-sufficiency = max_alpha H(Y_alpha | q(X)), coding cost = log2(|image(q)|), dynamical closure = 0, control regret = 0) is a two-element antichain: the constant map (min-coding-cost, max-task-sufficiency endpoint) and the true Z = joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) (unique zero-task-sufficiency frontier member). The identity is dominated by Z (same sufficiency 0, strictly higher coding cost 4 > 2) -- the static-case collapse of AF-2's 'segment from q* to identity' statement.

gates.AF1_FRONTIER_IS_ANTICHAIN: No two Pareto-set members weakly dominate each other on all four axes with strict inequality on at least one.
gates.AF1_FRONTIER_CONTAINS_TRUE_Z: joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) is a Pareto member.
gates.AF1_FRONTIER_CONTAINS_CONSTANT: The constant map is a Pareto member (min-coding-cost endpoint).
gates.AF1_IDENTITY_IS_DOMINATED_IN_STATIC_CASE: The identity is strictly dominated by joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) since both have task-sufficiency 0 and Z has strictly smaller coding cost.
gates.AF2_SUFFICIENT_FRONTIER_IS_TRUE_Z_ALONE: Among Pareto members with task-sufficiency 0, the only quotient is joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}).
gates.AF2_NO_PARETO_STRICTLY_FINER_THAN_TRUE_Z: No Pareto member is strictly finer than joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) on the lattice.

compute.sampling: exact enumeration of the 16-element Boolean world; no Monte Carlo
